_meta.purpose: Canonical MCP toolset shape shared by the stdio transport (cli/src/cli/mcp_server.py) and the backend Streamable HTTP transport (backend/app/mcp_server/tools.py, CHT-1266). cli/tests/test_mcp_toolset_sync.py asserts the stdio toolset matches this file exactly; backend/tests/test_mcp_toolset_sync.py asserts the HTTP toolset matches it for name/description and shared parameters, allowing only the documented additive 'team' parameter on issue_list/issue_create/doc_list/doc_create/activity_recent. Regenerate with cli/scripts/gen_mcp_toolset_schema.py if a stdio tool legitimately changes shape.

limit.description: Maximum number of activity entries to return.
limit.title: Limit

project.description: Restrict to one project (id, key, or name). Omit for team-wide activity.
project.title: Project

icon.description: Emoji or short icon label for the document.
icon.title: Icon

is_global.description: Create as a global/team-wide document instead of project-scoped.
is_global.title: Is Global

project.description: Project id, key, or name to attach to. Omit for the current project.
project.title: Project

doc_list.description: List documents (project-scoped by default, team-wide with all_projects=true).

all_projects.description: List every document in the team instead of just the current/given project.
all_projects.title: All Projects

limit.description: Maximum number of documents to return.
limit.title: Limit

project.description: Project id, key, or name to scope to. Defaults to the current project.

doc_update.description:
Update a document's title, content, icon, or project.

    Only the fields you pass are changed; omitted ones are left alone.
    Editing the title or content appends a new revision snapshot, so the
    prior version stays readable in the document's history -- an edit
    never destroys what it replaced.

content.description: New document body (markdown). Omit to leave unchanged.
content.title: Content

document_id.description: Document id, exact title, or id prefix.
document_id.title: Document Id

icon.description: New emoji or short icon label. Omit to leave unchanged.
icon.title: Icon

is_global.description: Make the document global/team-wide by detaching it from its project.
is_global.title: Is Global

project.description: Move the document to this project (id, key, or name).
project.title: Project

title.description: New document title. Omit to leave unchanged.
title.title: Title

doc_view.description: Show a document's content, comments, and linked issues.

document_id.description: Document id, exact title, or id prefix.
document_id.title: Document Id

issue_block.description:
Relate two issues: by default, `identifier` blocks `blocked`.

    Direction matters for `blocks` -- the issue named first is the one
    holding the other up, and it's the second one that stops showing up
    in issue_ready. Creating the same pair twice is a no-op, not an
    error.

blocked.description: The identifier of the issue on the other end of the relation, e.g. CHT-456.
blocked.title: Blocked

identifier.description: The blocking issue's identifier, e.g. CHT-123.
identifier.title: Identifier

relation_type.description: Relation to create. 'blocks': `identifier` blocks `blocked`. 'duplicates': `identifier` is a duplicate of `blocked`. 'relates_to': a plain association, no direction implied.
relation_type.title: Relation Type

issue_comment.description: Add a comment to an issue, optionally assigning it in the same call.

assign_to.description: Also assign the issue: 'me', a user/agent id, or a name/email.
assign_to.title: Assign To

issue_create.description: Create a new issue (optionally as a sub-issue of `parent`).

issue_type.description: Issue type. One of: task, bug, feature, chore, docs, tech_debt, refactor, epic (aliases accepted, e.g. 'feat').
issue_type.title: Issue Type

parent.description: Parent issue identifier (e.g. CHT-12) to create this as a sub-issue.
parent.title: Parent

project.description: Project id, key, or name. Defaults to the configured current project.
project.title: Project

issue_label.description:
Add and/or remove labels on an issue.

    Additive and subtractive rather than replacing the whole set, so
    labelling an issue never silently drops someone else's label. Labels
    must already exist (see label_list) -- this does not create them.

    Adding a label the issue already has, or removing one it doesn't
    have, is a no-op rather than an error, so the same call is safe to
    repeat.

add.description: Label names (or ids) to add. Names are matched case-insensitively.
add.title: Add

issue_list.description: List issues in a project (or team-wide with all_projects=true), with filters.

all_projects.description: List across every project in the team instead of just the current project. Ignored when `project` is passed explicitly; cannot be combined with `sprint`.
all_projects.title: All Projects

assignee.description: Filter by assignee: 'me', a user/agent id, or a name/email.
assignee.title: Assignee

epic.description: Filter to sub-issues of this epic/parent issue identifier (e.g. CHT-12).
epic.title: Epic

limit.description: Maximum number of issues to return.
limit.title: Limit

priority.description: Filter by one or more priorities (OR'd together).
priority.title: Priority

project.description: Project id, key, or name to list in. Defaults to the configured current project. Passing this always scopes to that one project, even if all_projects is also set.
project.title: Project

search.description: Free-text search over title, description, and identifier.
search.title: Search

sprint.description: Filter by sprint: a sprint name, 'current', 'next', or a sprint id.
sprint.title: Sprint

status.description: Filter by one or more statuses (OR'd together).
status.title: Status

issue_ready.description:
List issues that are open, unblocked, and unclaimed -- what you can start right now.

    Open + not-started (backlog/todo) only; excludes anything already
    in_progress/in_review/done/canceled, and excludes issues with an
    unresolved blocking relation. Priority-sorted (urgent first), then
    oldest first. Unassigned by default -- `mine` restricts to your own
    assigned-but-not-started work, `include_assigned` widens to every
    not-started issue regardless of assignee.

    Prefer this over issue_list when the question is "what should I pick
    up"; issue_list can filter by status and assignee but cannot express
    "has no unresolved blocker".

all_projects.description: Query across every project in the team instead of just the current/given one.
all_projects.title: All Projects

include_assigned.description: Widen beyond unassigned-only to include already-assigned (but not-started) issues.
include_assigned.title: Include Assigned

limit.description: Maximum number of issues to return.
limit.title: Limit

mine.description: Restrict to issues already assigned to you instead of unassigned ones.
mine.title: Mine

project.description: Project id, key, or name to scope to. Defaults to the current project.
project.title: Project

issue_relations.description:
Show an issue's relations: what it blocks, what blocks it, duplicates, and related work.

    Each relation carries a `direction` ("outgoing"/"incoming") and its
    own `id` -- pass that id to issue_unblock to remove it. Incoming
    `blocks` edges are reported as `blocked_by`, so the relation_type
    always reads from the perspective of the issue you asked about.

    Worth calling before issue_start: issue_view does not report
    blockers, so an issue can look startable there while being blocked.

issue_start.description:
Claim an issue: assign it to yourself and move it to in_progress.

    Equivalent to `chaotic issue start`.

issue_unblock.description:
Remove a relation between two issues.

    Name the other issue with `related` and the relation is looked up
    for you; pass `relation_id` from issue_relations when the two issues
    are connected by more than one relation.

    Removes only the relation -- neither issue is touched.

identifier.description: Issue identifier the relation hangs off, e.g. CHT-123.
identifier.title: Identifier

related.description: Identifier of the issue on the other end, e.g. CHT-456. Resolved to a relation automatically. Use relation_id instead if more than one relation connects the two.
related.title: Related

relation_id.description: Exact relation id from issue_relations. Takes precedence over `related`.
relation_id.title: Relation Id

issue_update.description:
Update an issue's status, priority, estimate, assignee, title, and/or description.

    Only fields explicitly passed are changed. Returns the updated issue.
    Pass `attest` to satisfy pending close/claim rituals in the same call.

assignee.description: New assignee: 'me', a user/agent id, a name/email, or 'unassigned' to clear it.
assignee.title: Assignee

attest.description: Ritual attestation notes to record BEFORE applying the update, as a map of ritual name -> note, e.g. {"close-gate": "ADR written", "doc-refresh": "README updated"}. Use when closing (status=done) or claiming (status=in_progress) a ticket whose rituals require notes — without them the status change is blocked by pending rituals (CHT-1326).
attest.title: Attest

issue_view.description: Show full issue detail: fields, description, comments, and sub-issues.

label_list.description:
List the team's labels: id, name, and color.

    The lookup that makes issue_list's `label` filter usable -- without
    it a caller has to already know the taxonomy to filter by it, or
    guess. Also the source of the names issue_label accepts.

project_list.description:
List the projects in your team: id, key, name, and issue count.

    The one call that answers "what projects exist" -- every other tool
    takes a `project` filter but none enumerate them. Scoped to the
    current team (`chaotic status`); the HTTP transport adds a `team`
    parameter for API keys that can see more than one.
